subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw add a public memorySearch exclusion contract now, and what scope should it cover across builtin indexing, QMD, index identity, status diagnostics, and docs?
rationale: The request adds or changes public memory-search configuration and recall-corpus semantics, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Repair and land the open excludePaths PR with merged default/per-agent semantics, index identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only documentation while tracking QMD and diagnostics separately.

options.title: Require cross-backend contract
options.body: Pause the open PR until builtin, QMD, watcher behavior, docs, status diagnostics, and stale-index cleanup share one exclusion model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and improve memory status/docs guidance around path drift, broad extraPaths, and benchmark contamination.

recommendation.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Repair and land the open excludePaths PR with merged default/per-agent semantics, index identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only documentation while tracking QMD and diagnostics separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-history signal for the memory host and index-identity boundary involved in the public config decision.
